title: Sosso Empire
capsule: The Sosso Empire was a Mande state in the western Sudan that rose to prominence after the collapse of the Ghana Empire, whose former vassal king Soumaoro Kanté (r. c. 1200–1235) conquered the Sahelian core including the old Ghanaian heartland. At its height Sosso dominated the upper Niger basin, exacting tribute from smaller polities through a feared cavalry force. Its reign was cut short at the Battle of Kirina (c. 1235), where the Mandinka prince Sundiata Keita, leading a coalition of tributary states, routed and killed Soumaoro. Sundiata's subsequent destruction of the Sosso capital absorbed its territory into the nascent Mali Empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of the Sosso Empire is poorly documented; modern scholarly maps reconstruct it from Arabic chronicles and oral tradition, and the precise borders are speculative.
